Definition: Illegitimately moving from 'every A has some B' to 'there is some B that fits every A'. Each person having something does not mean one thing serves everyone.
Example: Someone argues, 'Every student has a favorite teacher, so there is one teacher who is every student's favorite.'
FaithDiscussionExample: Someone argues, 'Every believer has a spiritual gift, so there is one gift every believer has.'
HowToRespond: Separate the two claims: 'Each person having something doesn't mean one thing serves everyone.'
